Measures
In this BFI data set, the 5 factors refer to the 5 composites included in the Big Five Inventory. Openness, which indicates one’s open-mindedness, creativity, and likelihood to embrace new experiences (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.6). Conscientiousness, which refers to one’s tendency to be reliable, organized, and disciplined (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.72). Extraversion, which refers to one’s social interactions and emotional expression (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.76). Agreeableness, which refers to one’s tendency to cooperate or desire to compete (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.7). and Neuroticism which refers to one’s tendency toward depression, anxiety, or negative feelings (Cronbach’s alpha =0.81).


Data Analysis Strategy
The data for variables O2, C4, E1, E2, and A1 were reverse keyed.

title: 9041 Assignment 2
text:
Introduction
This report examines the relationships between attachment-related anxiety, social anxiety, and self-esteem using survey data collected from adult participants. Three validated psychological scales were used to measure these constructs, and scores were compared across the full sample as well as a filtered subsample.

Methods

Measures
Participants completed three self-report questionnaires measuring attachment-related anxiety, social anxiety, and self-esteem.
Social Interaction Anxiety Scale (SIAS). This 20-item scale measures anxiety experienced during social interactions. In this sample, the scale showed good internal consistency (α = 0.9024323).
Experiences in Close Relationships Scale (shortened Attachment-Related Anxiety subscale). This 9-item subscale measures attachment-related anxiety in close relationships. In this sample, internal consistency was excellent (α = 0.937966).
Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (RSES). This 10-item scale measures global self-esteem. In this sample, the scale showed good internal consistency (α = 0.8457738).


Data Analysis Strategy
Prior to scoring, raw survey responses were cleaned and converted to integer values. Scale scores were then calculated using the scoreItems() function from the psych package, which computes average item scores and Cronbach’s alpha for each scale.
Reverse-keying was applied to items worded in the opposite direction of the construct being measured, so that higher scores consistently reflect higher levels of the trait across all items. For the Social Interaction Anxiety Scale, items 5, 9, and 11 were reverse-keyed. For the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale, items 2, 5, 6, 8, and 9 were reverse-keyed, consistent with the scale’s standard scoring procedure in which several items are worded positively (e.g., “I feel I have a number of good qualities”) rather than negatively. No items on the Experiences in Close Relationships Anxiety subscale required reverse-keying.
